descriptors.concept_name: Overview of Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements
descriptors.definition: Consolidated financial statements display the combined financial position and operating results of a parent company and its controlled subsidiaries. In contrast, separate financial statements reflect the financial position of a single individual reporting entity.
inclusion: Financial position of a parent and its group companies
Financial position of a single entity
nearby_distinctions: Consolidated financial statements present an entire group overview under parent control, whereas separate financial statements focus solely on a single legal entity.

descriptors.concept_name: Overview of Indian Accounting Standards for Group Entities
descriptors.definition: Various Indian Accounting Standards govern the accounting, control evaluation, and disclosure requirements for group entities, joint arrangements, and investments in associates. These standards prescribe specific procedures for consolidation, equity accounting, and separate financial statement reporting.
inclusion: Consolidated financial statements criteria and procedures
Investments in associates and joint ventures
Separate financial statements accounting and disclosures
Disclosures of interests in other entities
nearby_distinctions: Ind AS 110 handles subsidiary control and consolidation, whereas Ind AS 27 specifically regulates accounting and disclosures in separate financial statements.
